subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC qualification - follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Reed <danielle.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC qualification - follow-up

Hi Danielle -

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can prepare the lab test and sizing guidance for Acme Health's private deployment:

Summary from the call:
- SLO targets: P95 latency <= 120ms for streaming text generation (avg prompt ~150 tokens), P99 <= 300ms for single-turn non-streaming calls.
- Expected peak throughput: ~350 requests/minute with burst to 1k RPM during business hours.
- Concurrency target: 60 concurrent streams (long-lived).
- Preferred model: open LLM family you mentioned (cust-provided) - we need model size and tokenization details to validate memory/KV cache sizing.
- Network: private VPC peering preferred; you asked about VPN fallback for initial rollout.

Follow-ups / action items:
1) Can you share a network diagram showing VPC boundaries, peering/VPN endpoints, and any egress inspection/proxy (even a simple diagram is fine)?
2) Do you have an internal latency budget for calls between your app servers and the Redwood Private edge? Specifically, target RTT or max hop count.
3) Confirm whether outbound egress must traverse an HTTP proxy or TLS inspection device (this affects TLS session and streaming performance).
4) Any constraints on opening outbound ports for peering (we typically need TCP 443 and some UDP for health checks, details below).

If you can attach the network diagram and a point person for infra (VPN/Networking), Marissa and I will put together a test plan with a canary throughput profile and a network pre-check checklist.

Thanks -
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan / Marissa -

Thanks - attaching our network diagram (see attachment). A few answers inline:

- Network diagram: attached (acmehealth-network-diagram.pdf) - shows VPCs, transit gateway, and the primary VPN termination point.
- Latency budgets: Our internal SLA for platform-to-backend calls is P95 < 80ms within the same region. For calls crossing our transit gateway to a partner VPC we budget P95 < 160ms.
- Egress inspection: Yes, some environments have a TLS inspection appliance on egress for logging. We can provision a dedicated path that bypasses inspection for Redwood traffic if needed but it requires a ticket.
- Ports: We can open TCP 443 for peering and allow outbound to your IP range. UDP not likely an option in our security posture right now.

Attaching: acmehealth-network-diagram.pdf (attachment: acmehealth-network-diagram.pdf - application/pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Danielle -

Appreciate the diagram and the latency budget details - that's very helpful. A few follow-ups/questions so our infra team (Marissa) can size correctly and design the pre-checks:

1) TLS inspection bypass: Great to hear there's a possible dedicated path. If you can provision that, it will significantly improve streaming stability. Can you estimate the lead time to get a bypass ticket approved?

2) UDP health checks: we can avoid UDP by switching to TCP health checks/HTTP probes if that's required. Confirming: TCP 443 allowed outbound is sufficient?

3) Concurrency semantics: you noted 60 concurrent streams. Are those long-lived bi-directional streams (e.g., WebSocket/RPC) held for multiple seconds/minutes? If so, what's the median duration? This helps with connection pool sizing and keepalive config.

4) Throughput profile: 350 RPM steady, 1k RPM burst - can you share expected burst duration (minutes) and whether bursts are uniformly distributed or concentrated in short windows?

Proposed test plan (high level):
- Phase 0: Network pre-check (ping/trace, TCP 443 handshake times from representative app host to our peering endpoint).
- Phase 1: Small concurrency test (10 concurrent streams, streaming model) to validate tail latency and keepalive behavior.
- Phase 2: Ramp to target concurrency (60) and steady throughput (350 RPM) for a 30m soak.
- Phase 3: Burst test to 1k RPM for 5 minutes, observe backpressure and P99 latency.

Marissa - added you to keep this in perf lane. Can you confirm if these phases map to what you need and if the soak/burst durations look right?

Thanks,
Jordan

On the attachment: acmehealth-network-diagram.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Reed <danielle.reed@acmehealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Private VPC qualification - follow-up

Hi Danielle / Jordan -

Thanks for the diagram and the details, Danielle. Quick responses and a clear next-step proposal from our side:

Answers/notes:
- TCP 443-only is OK; we'll switch our health checks to TCP/HTTP probes. UDP health checks are not required.
- TLS inspection bypass: if Acme can provision a bypass path for Redwood traffic that will reduce observed tail latency; if the bypass takes time, we can still run the tests but expect slightly higher P99s on streaming.
- For long-lived streams: please confirm median stream duration; if streams exceed ~30s on average we recommend keepalive of 20s and an idle timeout of 90s on the connection pool.

Sizing recommendations (prelim):
- For 60 concurrent streams and target throughput (~350 RPM steady), we recommend a Private edge with 8 vGPU workers (A100-class equivalent) configured with continuous batching and KV cache shard size tuned to the model's KV footprint.
- Memory/CPU: assume ~6GB GPU memory per worker reserved for KV cache plus model inference; we will refine once you share model size.

Proposed timeline & next steps:
1) Acme to confirm: TLS bypass lead time, median stream duration, and model artifact (or model name + size).
2) Redwood to run Phase 0 tests (network pre-check). We will provide a small test harness (curl-based and streaming client) and IP ranges to allow.
3) Once pre-check passes, schedule Phase 1 on a Wednesday morning (low traffic) - allow 2 hours for the initial soak and review.

I've uploaded a short network pre-check checklist and the test harness link here: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/ACME-network-test-plan.
HubSpot record: HS-12345.

If that all sounds good, Danielle, can you confirm the network lead and preferred calendar windows for the Phase 0 pre-check?

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Director, Performance & Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
